citation.authors: S. Yoon, M. Sorbaro Sindaci, A. V. Goltsev, J. F. F. Mendes
citation.title: Critical behavior of the relaxation rate, the susceptibility, and a pair correlation function in the Kuramoto model on scale-free networks

why_this_source: The paper that defines BOTH observables side by side in one text, and the one that says what a lab measuring d<r>/dh should expect: exponent 1 on both sides, with an amplitude ratio of 2.
observable: BOTH, kept separate: chi(h) = dr(h)/dh (field response) and C~(h) = N[<z z*>_t - <z>_t<z*>_t] (fluctuation).
frequency_class: None. These are thermodynamic-limit mean-field results on a Lorentzian g — no finite-N sampling class enters at all.

quotes.locator: Sec. V, the definition of the susceptibility
quotes.quote:
We define the susceptibility as follows:
chi(h) == d r(h)/dh,
where the order parameter r(h) must be found taking into account the field h. This definition is similar to the longitudinal susceptibility in the classical XY model.
quotes.bears_on: The FIELD-response observable, defined explicitly and separately from the fluctuation in the same paper. This is the object K03's instrument measures.

quotes.locator: definition of the pair correlation function
quotes.bears_on: The FLUCTUATION observable, in the same paper, under a different symbol.

quotes.locator: Sec. on the pair correlation function; ref [15] = H. Daido, J. Stat. Phys. 60, 753 (1990)
quotes.quote: Numerical simulations in [28, 15, 29] revealed that C~ has a sharp maximum at the critical coupling Kc. Using an analytical approach in [15], Daido found that C~ proportional to |K-Kc|^{-gamma'} with the critical exponent gamma'=1 when K<Kc and gamma'=1/4 when K>Kc.
quotes.bears_on: Second independent attribution of the 1/4-and-1 pair to Daido JSP 1990, and confirmation it sits on C~ (the fluctuation), not on their chi (the response).

quotes.locator: Table I, rows for degree exponent > 5 (finite fourth moment; includes the complete graph), Lorentzian g
quotes.bears_on: WHAT A FIELD-RESPONSE MEASUREMENT SHOULD RETURN: exponent 1 on both sides, with an AMPLITUDE ratio of exactly 2. An amplitude ratio is not an exponent asymmetry, and mistaking one for the other is a live hazard.

quotes.locator: Sec. VII (Simulations), closing sentence of the pair-correlation paragraph
quotes.quote: However, further theoretical analysis and more detailed simulations of larger networks are necessary to prove this suggestion.
quotes.bears_on: The one FDT-like fluctuation-equals-response identity on offer in this literature is flagged as unproven by its own authors.

numbers: FIELD RESPONSE | mean field, Lorentzian, no sampling class | chi(0) = (1/2)(1 - K/K_c)^(-1) below and (1/4)(K/K_c - 1)^(-1) above. Exponent 1 both sides; amplitude ratio 2.
FIELD RESPONSE | at K = K_c: r ~ h^(1/3), chi(h) ~ h^(-2/3).
caveats: Their C(h) is the variance of the LONGITUDINAL PROJECTION of z measured in a FINITE field that pins the phase — not N*Var(|z|) at h = 0. At h = 0 the Kuramoto phase diffuses freely, so the two are different objects.
Their symbol gamma is the network degree exponent, not a susceptibility exponent.
